learningObjective: Contrast template-based schedule search (AutoTVM) and template-free schedule search (Ansor / MetaSchedule).
stem: AutoTVM (template-based) and Ansor (template-free) both search for a good schedule of a tensor program, but they differ in what constitutes the search space. Which contrast is correct?

options.text: Both approaches use the same search space; the only difference is the choice of measurement backend (simulator vs. real hardware).
Template-based search learns the template from data; template-free search enumerates all schedules exhaustively.

Template-based search requires the developer to write a schedule template with parameter placeholders (tile size, unroll factor, thread bindings); the search explores parameter combinations of a fixed template. Template-free search generates candidate schedules by combining schedule primitives directly from the tensor expression, requiring no manual template but enlarging the search space.
Template-free search always outperforms template-based search on every workload; the two are strictly dominated.

explanation: Template-based schedule search (AutoTVM) relies on a developer-authored schedule template with tunable parameters; the search explores those parameters. This produces a small, focused search space but requires per-operator template engineering. Template-free search (Ansor, MetaSchedule) constructs candidate schedules automatically by composing schedule primitives (split, tile, bind, unroll, vectorize) directly from the compute definition; this eliminates manual template work at the cost of a much larger search space, which is why learned cost models and evolutionary search become important. B misattributes 'learned template' to template-based. C claims equal search spaces which is inaccurate. D over-generalizes; on templated workloads AutoTVM can be competitive or better within its narrow space.

optionExplanations.B: Wrong: template-based does not learn templates; humans write them.
optionExplanations.C: Correct: matches the definitions in the TVM/AutoTVM and Ansor papers.
optionExplanations.D: Wrong: template-based can win on well-templated workloads with less tuning budget.

assumptions: The two systems are compared with equivalent compilation and measurement budgets in principle.
The operators being tuned admit valid schedule templates.
nonImplications: Does not imply template-free search is always faster to converge; the larger space needs more measurements.
Does not imply template-free eliminates all human input — the compute definition and cost-model features are still designed.

distractorRationales.B: Confuses template authorship with template learning.
